metadata.name: Angina pectoris (stable)
metadata.emergency_level: Stable angina is routine; UNSTABLE angina / acute coronary syndrome is an emergency
metadata.severity: Chronic; marker of coronary disease with risk of myocardial infarction

overview.short_description: Chest discomfort due to myocardial ischaemia (usually from coronary atherosclerosis), classically brought on by exertion or emotion and relieved by rest or GTN; a manifestation of coronary artery disease.
overview.detailed_description: Stable angina is predictable, exertional chest discomfort from a mismatch between myocardial oxygen supply and demand, usually due to fixed coronary stenosis. The essential task is to distinguish stable angina (managed as chronic coronary disease) from an acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina/myocardial infarction), which is an emergency. Management combines anti-anginal drugs, secondary-prevention therapy, risk-factor control, and revascularisation in selected patients.
overview.pathophysiology: Coronary atherosclerosis limits blood flow; during increased demand (exertion), oxygen supply cannot meet myocardial demand, producing transient ischaemia and pain that resolves with rest/reduced demand or nitrate-induced vasodilation.
overview.etiology: Coronary atherosclerosis (overwhelmingly); also aortic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, coronary spasm (Prinzmetal), and increased demand states (anaemia, thyrotoxicosis) or reduced supply (severe anaemia).
overview.natural_history: Chronic; may be stable for years, but coronary disease can progress or plaques rupture causing acute coronary syndromes.
overview.prognosis: Variable; good with risk-factor control and treatment, but reflects underlying coronary disease with ongoing cardiovascular risk.

prevalence.value: Common; increases with age and cardiovascular risk factors.

incidence.value: Rises with age; higher with diabetes, smoking, hypertension, dyslipidaemia.

mortality.value: Coronary artery disease is a leading global cause of death.

epidemiology.age_groups: Middle-aged and older adults; earlier with strong risk factors/FH.
epidemiology.sex_predominance: More common/earlier in men; women may present atypically.

risk_factors.diabetes: Major risk factor; may cause atypical/silent ischaemia.
risk_factors.pregnancy: Uncommon; consider other causes of chest pain.
risk_factors.occupation: Physically or emotionally demanding work may provoke symptoms.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Dyslipidaemia, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, prior cardiovascular disease.

chief_complaints.complaint: Chest tightness/pressure on exertion, eased by rest
Pain radiating to the arm, neck or jaw

chief_complaints.importance: May be an anginal equivalent (esp. diabetics/women)

symptoms.symptom: Relieved by rest or GTN within ~5 minutes
Prolonged rest pain, pain at rest, or rapidly worsening symptoms
symptoms.importance: RED FLAG - unstable angina / acute coronary syndrome

negative_findings.finding: Pain clearly pleuritic, positional, reproduced by palpation, or fleeting
negative_findings.why_important: Makes cardiac angina much less likely (suggests musculoskeletal/other cause)

negative_findings.finding: No rest pain, no crescendo pattern, haemodynamically stable

history_questions.question: Is the discomfort constricting/central, brought on by exertion, and relieved by rest or GTN?
history_questions.why_ask: The three features define typical/atypical/non-anginal pain

history_questions.question: Is there pain at rest, prolonged pain, or rapidly worsening episodes?
Cardiovascular risk factors (smoking, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, family history)?
Any breathlessness, palpitations, or exertional syncope?
history_questions.why_ask: Consider heart failure, arrhythmia, aortic stenosis

history_questions.question: How limiting are the symptoms (activities that trigger them)?

physical_examination.examination: Cardiovascular exam (pulses, BP, murmurs, heart failure signs)
physical_examination.expected_finding: Often normal; aortic stenosis murmur or heart-failure signs alter the picture

physical_examination.examination: Chest wall palpation (to help exclude musculoskeletal cause)
physical_examination.expected_finding: Cardiac pain is NOT reproduced by palpation

vital_signs.blood_pressure: Often raised (comorbid); check for aortic stenosis effects

laboratory_tests.indication: ONLY if acute coronary syndrome suspected (not for stable angina work-up)

imaging.imaging_type: CT coronary angiography (first-line for chest pain of suspected cardiac origin, NICE CG95)
Functional imaging (stress echo, perfusion MRI/SPECT) / invasive angiography
imaging.when_needed: Assess ischaemia or when CTCA uncertain / for revascularisation planning

ecg.when_needed: Resting ECG in all with suspected angina; urgent ECG if ACS suspected
ecg.findings: Often normal in stable angina; may show prior MI/ischaemia; ST changes/ischaemia in ACS.

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Not applicable (consider GI causes if atypical)
other_diagnostic_tests.exercise_testing: Historically used; NICE now favours CT coronary angiography / functional imaging

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Assess chest pain by three features: (1) constricting discomfort in chest/neck/shoulders/jaw/arms; (2) precipitated by exertion; (3) relieved by rest or GTN within ~5 minutes. All three = typical angina; two = atypical; one or none = non-anginal. Investigate suspected angina (e.g., CT coronary angiography per NICE CG95). Distinguish from acute coronary syndrome (rest/prolonged/crescendo pain).

differential_diagnosis.differences: Pain at rest, prolonged, crescendo, associated sweating/nausea, ECG/troponin changes
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the pain occurring at rest, prolonged, or getting rapidly worse?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Related to meals/lying down, burning, not exertional
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is it burning, related to meals rather than exertion?
Can you reproduce it by pressing or moving?
Any exertional blackouts and a heart murmur?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Pulmonary embolism / other acute chest pathology
differential_diagnosis.differences: Pleuritic, risk factors, hypoxia, sudden onset
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Sudden pleuritic pain with breathlessness and risk factors?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the pain occurring at rest, lasting a long time, or rapidly worsening?
Does the discomfort come on with exertion and settle with rest/GTN within a few minutes?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Exertional + relief by rest/GTN -> typical angina

next_best_question.question: Any rest/prolonged pain (ACS), what are the anginal features, and what is your cardiovascular risk?
next_best_question.expected_answers: ACS features vs stable angina pattern
next_best_question.branching_logic: ACS features -> emergency admission; stable pattern -> resting ECG, investigate (CT coronary angiography), start anti-anginal + secondary prevention

next_best_test.expected_outcome: May show prior MI/ischaemia; guides risk

next_best_test.why: First-line to diagnose stable coronary disease (NICE CG95)

red_flags.finding: Chest pain at rest, prolonged (>15-20 min), or rapidly worsening (crescendo), especially with sweating/nausea
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - call emergency services; treat as acute coronary syndrome (aspirin, ECG, urgent transfer)

red_flags.finding: Haemodynamic instability, syncope, or signs of heart failure with chest pain
Exertional syncope with a murmur (aortic stenosis)
red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent cardiology assessment; avoid provocative exertion

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (emergency); new/unstable or rapidly worsening angina; suspected significant valvular disease.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Confirmed/suspected stable angina for investigation and optimisation; refractory symptoms for revascularisation assessment.

early: Progression to acute coronary syndrome/myocardial infarction

initial_management.supportive_care: Explain the diagnosis and the difference from a heart attack; provide a GTN action plan (repeat once after 5 min; if not relieved, call emergency services).
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Short-acting nitrate; Beta-blocker; Calcium-channel blocker; Aspirin/antiplatelet; Statin. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG126, NICE_NG238.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Stop smoking, healthy diet, regular activity within limits, weight management, manage stress, treat exacerbating factors (anaemia, thyroid).
initial_management.follow_up: Review symptom control and secondary-prevention adherence; escalate if symptoms worsen.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Symptom relief: sublingual GTN for episodes; a beta-blocker or calcium-channel blocker first-line, with additional anti-anginals (long-acting nitrate, ivabradine, nicorandil, ranolazine) as needed. Secondary prevention for everyone: antiplatelet (aspirin), high-intensity statin, and address BP/diabetes; ACE inhibitor if indicated. Consider revascularisation (PCI/CABG) for suitable patients with limiting symptoms or high-risk disease.

patient_education.home_advice: Angina is chest discomfort from narrowed heart arteries, usually brought on by exertion and eased by rest. Carry your GTN spray: if you get an attack, stop and rest and use it; if the pain is not gone after a second dose 5 minutes later, call the emergency services - it could be a heart attack. Take your heart-protecting medicines every day, stop smoking, and stay active within your limits.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: الذبحة الصدرية انزعاج في الصدر من ضيق شرايين القلب، تظهر غالباً مع الجهد وتزول بالراحة. احمل بخاخ النتروجليسرين (GTN): عند النوبة توقّف واسترح واستخدمه، وإن لم يزُل الألم بعد جرعة ثانية بعد 5 دقائق فاتّصل بالإسعاف - فقد تكون نوبة قلبية. تناول أدوية حماية القلب يومياً، وتوقّف عن التدخين، وحافظ على النشاط ضمن حدودك.
patient_education.prevention: Risk-factor control (smoking, BP, cholesterol, diabetes), healthy lifestyle; secondary-prevention medication.
patient_education.warning_signs: Chest pain at rest, lasting more than a few minutes, not relieved by GTN, or with sweating/nausea/breathlessness - call emergency services.

prevention.vaccination: Influenza vaccination recommended in cardiovascular disease.
prevention.lifestyle: Smoking cessation, healthy diet, activity, weight and stress management.
prevention.screening: Cardiovascular risk assessment; manage risk factors.

evidence.evidence_level: High for secondary prevention and anti-anginal therapy; strong evidence base for investigation pathways.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_CG126, NICE_NG238; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE CG95/CG126, ESC chronic coronary syndromes.
